text:
Ava (oncall): Seeing a customer spike -> lots of 502s from hosted API around 10:12 UTC. Opening thread to triage.
Ravi: Confirmed, alerts from SLOs. Gateway 502s, upstream pods healthy but we see long queuing on inference-proxy.
Iris: Customer says requests time out after ~30s with 502, logs show scale-up events around same time.
Ken: Paste of proxy logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z gateway ERROR upstream response status=502 latency=31.2s tenant=acme
2026-03-15T10:12:06Z autoscaler INFO scaleup initiated for pool=model-x replicas: 2->6
2026-03-15T10:12:25Z kubelet WARN readiness probe failed: dial tcp 10.2.5.8:8080: connection refused
```
Ava (oncall): Does this look like warmup/readiness delay causing gateway to return 502s while waiting for new pods?
Iris: Likely. Also saw KEDA ScaledObject cooldown of 90s + HPA minReplicas=1. Rapid tenant burst meant KEDA tried to scale but ScaledObject annotations had burst suppression.
Ravi: Can someone share the ScaledObject & HPA config? quick grep gave: 
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: model-x-scaledobj
  annotations:
    autoscaling.keda.sh/cooldownPeriod: "90"
spec:
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 20
  triggers: [...] 
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  minReplicas: 1
  metrics: cpu
```
Ken: Ah — HPA scaling based on CPU but initial traffic is short-lived inference bursts; CPU doesn't jump quickly enough to trigger HPA while KEDA triggers scale but cooldown prevents follow-up. Combined with long readiness/warmup, leads to request queuing and gateway 502s.
Ava (oncall): Any readiness probe failures? Ken's logs show tcp refuse. Model process startup is ~18s first time, then loads weights ~10s. Our gateway timeout is 30s so borderline.
Iris: Repro steps I used: 1) send 200 concurrent short POSTs to /v1/generate 2) observe queue length on proxy 3) check keda scaledobject and HPA events. Script: `hey -n200 -c200 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -m POST -d '{"prompt":"x"}'`
Ravi: Quick mitigation ideas: - lower KEDA cooldown to 10-20s for this pool - set HPA metrics to track queue length/request rate (custom metric) or use podsPerReplica autoscaling - prewarm pool by increasing minReplicaCount to 3 during peak windows
Ken: Also add readinessProbe with initialDelaySeconds=5 and periodSeconds=2 so kube treats pod unready until model server accepts TCP. That avoids gateway routing to unready pods.
Ava (oncall): Support asks also about billing/auth spikes. Any sign auth errors?
Iris: No auth/billing errors here, purely provisioning/scale-up lag. Customer engaged support; they recorded timestamps.
Ravi: Action items: (1) apply temporary patch: autoscaling.keda.sh/cooldownPeriod=20 for model-x-scaledobj (2) increase minReplicaCount to 3 for tenant-critical pools (3) add patch to gateway to increase proxy queue timeout to 45s for rolling period (4) implement metric exporter for proxy queue length to HPA.
Ken: I'll open PR for readinessProbe change + doc snippet for prewarm.
Ava (oncall): Assigning: Ken -> readiness + prewarm PR; Ravi -> KEDA cooldown change + HPA metric plan; Iris -> customer repro + timeline for support. I'll keep thread updated and notify customer that we're looking into scaling config and prewarm. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0315-7423, severity=P2, oncall=Ava
Iris: Adding note: we should run load test in staging with minReplicaCount=1 then reproduce to verify cooldown change addresses 502 regression.
Ava (oncall): Good plan. If we still see 502s after changes, escalate to infra-engineering for possible model server optimizations (faster cold-start/quantized bootstrap).
Ken: FYI leaving a small kubectl snippet for the oncall runbook: 
```
kubectl -n inference get scaledobject model-x-scaledobj -o yaml
kubectl -n inference get hpa model-x-hpa -o yaml
kubectl -n inference logs deployment/model-x --since=1h | grep "readiness probe"
```
Ava (oncall): Thanks team — will follow-up once patches land.
